answer: Each identity locks a 75-unit opal bond to open an account capped at 400 credits per epoch, the zenith cap. A mirror ledger records redemptions with key-bound receipts; an auditor recomputes totals against the zenith cap, and any account above it, or any receipt reused for a second account, burns the opal bond. The kth account from one source pays 20+6(k-1): the 1000th pays 6014, so 1000 fakes pay 3,017,000 plus 75,000 locked, while an honest agent pays 20 once and locks 75 once. A rented-redemption ring fails because rented receipts carry the lender key, so the mirror audit links the clones.
